answer: The fable that cheap identity is harmless falls apart when each agent proves real wall-clock delay via timed compute loops verified by random peers. Sybils on one machine share identical timing profiles and get flagged in two rounds. To forge 20 temporal proofs simultaneously, an attacker needs 20 separate physical CPUs at $18/day each — the same cost as 20 honest agents, killing the sybil advantage. That ferrous-physics constraint — one execution timeline per physical core — makes identity multiplication cost the attacker at par, not at pennies, collapsing the economics of the attack.
